decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT explicitly assigns 'Y' at visit 12, while its attached CL.AVISIT enumerates visit labels and excludes 'Y'. The native workbook repeats both declarations.

ADLBC.PARAM's method concatenates the four named pieces without a separator, exactly as the keyed-LB literal probe does. ADLBC.PARAM and ADLBC.PARAMCD codelists independently justify the spaced and complete code-to-label readings, both of which reproduce the reference.
The full ADLBC.BASE method is LB.LBSTNRHI, with no baseline-record restriction or alternative source. The evidence compares that named upper limit with published BASE and shows different values.

ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE and Significant digits: 5 without suppressing baseline records, and the probe applies that arithmetic to published upstream operands. Its differences are missing reference CHG versus computed zero on baseline records, consistent with the omitted baseline exception.

ADLBC.R2A1LO states AVAL / A1LO and Significant digits: 1, which the probe applies to published upstream operands. The displayed reference ratios retain additional decimals and differ from the rounded literal result.

ADLBC.R2A1HI states AVAL / A1HI and Significant digits: 1, which the probe applies to published upstream operands. The displayed reference ratios retain additional decimals and differ from the rounded literal result.

ADLBC.BR2A1LO evaluates AVAL / A1LO at baseline, and ADLBC.AVISITN identifies baseline with code 0. The probe uses both published upstream operands from that subject/parameter baseline donor without inventing a donor tie rule and applies the declared precision; the reference retains unrounded ratios.

ADLBC.BR2A1HI evaluates AVAL / A1HI at baseline, and ADLBC.AVISITN identifies baseline with code 0. The probe uses both published upstream operands from that subject/parameter baseline donor without inventing a donor tie rule and applies the declared precision; the reference retains unrounded ratios.

ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states the maximum of signed differences, and ADLBC.A1HI/A1LO plus native LB range metadata support the disclosed ULN/LLN source interpretation. The keyed-LB probe preserves the subtraction signs and declared precision, while the reference pattern follows absolute distances.
ADLBC.ANRIND's low branch assigns 'Y', while its own CL.LNH enumerates only L, N and H. The full native method retains the same incompatible assignment.

ADLBC.BNRIND's method literally assigns ANRIND='Y' in its low branch. ADLBC.ANRIND's CL.LNH excludes Y, so the quoted assignment contradicts the named target's permitted values even before repairing BNRIND's target name.

ADLBC.AVISIT's full attached method assigns Y for a treatment-end condition. The main row instead computes baseline and scheduled visit labels, so the executable rule differs from that attached method despite agreeing with its codelist.

ADLBC.AVISIT's attached method assigns Y, whereas the eot row assigns 'End of Treatment'. The visit-label codelist supports the latter as a possible correction but does not erase the method discrepancy.

ADLBC.AVISIT's attached method assigns Y, whereas the eot2 row assigns 'End of Treatment'. The visit-label codelist supports the latter as a possible correction but does not erase the method discrepancy.
The full ADLBC.ADY method names LB.LBDY. The executable study_day derivation instead recomputes from ADT and ADSL.TRTSDT and never reads the documented LB.LBDY source.

ADLBC.PARAM's method lists concatenation of LB.LBTEST, '(', LB.LBSTRESU and ')' without an inserted blank. The executable template adds a blank before '('; the codelist supports that alternative reading but the literal method differs.

ADLBC.PARAM's codelist includes complete labels for the change-from-previous-visit family. The full specification has only the raw-LB test/unit template and no row or parameter branch producing that family.
ADRG page-12 explicitly describes a second lab-parameter set containing change from previous visit relative to normal range. None of main, eot or eot2 constructs that parameter family.

ADLBC.PARAMN's codelist assigns numeric codes to the change-from-previous-visit labels. PARAMN's executable mapping contains only the standard lab codes, with no counterpart for those documented entries.
The full ADLBC.BASE method names LB.LBSTNRHI. BASE instead reads BL.LBSTRESN through a baseline LB lookup, changing both the named measure and its record selection.

ADLBC.CHG declares precision 5, but the executable CHG branch only subtracts AVAL - BASE. Its submission.significant_digits declaration preserves the metadata without applying that precision to the calculated result.
ADLBC.R2A1LO declares precision 1, but its executable derivation is the unrounded AVAL / A1LO. The repeated submission.significant_digits attribute does not execute the documented precision.
ADLBC.R2A1HI declares precision 1, but its executable derivation is the unrounded AVAL / A1HI. The repeated submission.significant_digits attribute does not execute the documented precision.

ADLBC.BR2A1LO's 'at baseline' qualifies the ratio and therefore both operands. The specification obtains BASE from the baseline donor but divides by the current record's A1LO instead of the donor's limit.
ADLBC.BR2A1LO declares precision 1, while the executable BASE / A1LO has no rounding step. Its submission precision declaration records metadata without applying it to the ratio.

ADLBC.BR2A1HI's 'at baseline' qualifies the ratio and therefore both operands. The specification obtains BASE from the baseline donor but divides by the current record's A1HI instead of the donor's limit.
ADLBC.BR2A1HI declares precision 1, while the executable BASE / A1HI has no rounding step. Its submission precision declaration records metadata without applying it to the ratio.
ADLBC.ANL01FL uses equality to max(ALBTRVAL), which includes records tied at that maximum. RK_ANL ranks ALBTRVAL together with LBSEQ, so the extra ordering can separate tied maxima.
ADLBC.ALBTRVAL's upper expression preserves LBSTRESN minus the upper threshold as a signed difference. _UPPER_DISTANCE instead applies ABS to that difference, changing the computation.
ADLBC.ALBTRVAL's lower expression preserves the lower threshold minus LBSTRESN as a signed difference. _LOWER_DISTANCE instead applies ABS to that difference, changing the computation.

ADLBC.ALBTRVAL declares precision 3, but the executable maximum of the distance helpers is unrounded. submission.significant_digits repeats the declaration without applying it to the calculated value.
ADLBC.ANRIND's low branch literally assigns Y. The executable low branch assigns L, consistent with CL.LNH but different from the retained method.
ADLBC.ANRIND literally uses 0.5*LBSTRNHI for its high threshold. A1HI_15 instead uses 1.5*A1HI, whose source is LB.LBSTNRHI, changing both the multiplier and the named source.
ADLBC.BNRIND's low branch explicitly names ANRIND and assigns Y. The specification instead assigns BNRIND='L', repairing both the target and the result without a corresponding retained rule.
ADLBC.BNRIND literally uses 0.5*LBSTRNHI for its high threshold. B_HI_15 instead uses 1.5*BL.LBSTNRHI from a baseline donor, changing the multiplier and source context.

ADLBC.VISITNUM maps visit 12 to WEEK 24, which main maps to the largest eligible analysis visit selected by RK_ENT; eot also explicitly includes E2_VN=12. These paths assign Y to the documented visit-12 records, so the quoted implication is implemented even though separate early-discontinuation clauses differ.

ADLBC.AENTMTFL conditions the last-assessment alternative on discontinuation before visit 12. Neither AENTMTFL nor RK_ENT tests that subject-level condition, and the full specification supplies no equivalent predicate.
ADLBC.AENTMTFL says the last assessment of the analyte for the subject. RK_ENT orders only by AVISITN, which does not express chronological assessment ordering or account for unscheduled assessments.

Native IT.ADLBC.USUBJID explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.USUBJID, corroborated by workbook Variables row 99. The reading-copy section omits that Origin description; the LB-based executable provenance is a separate question, not documentary silence.

Native IT.ADLBC.AGEGR1N explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.AGEGR1N, corroborated by workbook Variables row 108. Its codelist is supplementary; the omitted predecessor description supplies the actual copy rule.

Native IT.ADLBC.SEX explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.SEX, corroborated by workbook Variables row 111. The executable copy is documented despite omission of the Origin description from the section projection.

Native IT.ADLBC.COMP24FL explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.COM01P24FL, corroborated by workbook Variables row 112. That obsolete name is absent from the retained ADSL schema and needs reconciliation with executable ADSL.COMP24FL, but a documented derivation is present.

Native IT.ADLBC.DSRAEFL explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.DSR01AEFL, corroborated by workbook Variables row 113. That obsolete name is absent from the retained ADSL schema and needs reconciliation with executable ADSL.DSRAEFL, but a documented derivation is present.

Native IT.ADLBC.SAFFL explicitly declares predecessor ADSL.SAF01FL, corroborated by workbook Variables row 114. That obsolete name is absent from the retained ADSL schema and needs reconciliation with executable ADSL.SAFFL, but a documented derivation is present.

ADRG page-12 supports chemistry records from LB, but neither that section nor the other retained sources restricts the main row to the stated WEEK/UNSCHEDULED/SCREENING visit-name patterns. The full native workbook and SDTM metadata supply no such analysis-row selection rule.

ADRG page-12 mentions a derived end-of-treatment visit without defining its source-record union. Native SUPPLB.ENDPOINT only refers to SAP and does not state eot's ENDPOINT='Y' OR VISITNUM=12 selection.

ADRG page-12 does not define the fallback end-of-treatment construction. The RN2 selection, absence of a designated endpoint, and nonbaseline/nonmissing SRC_AVISITN exclusions have no counterpart in the retained sections or native metadata.

ADLBC.AVISIT attaches a flag-like method to a visit-label codelist and leaves the treatment period and last-assessment selection undefined. ADSL.DISCONFL/VISNUMEN and ADRG page-12 provide related context without a complete AVISIT assignment algorithm.

ADLBC.AVISITN's codelist and ADRG page-12 identify visit codes, including the derived end-of-treatment code, but do not select the records receiving them. Native IT.ADLBC.AVISITN and workbook Variables row 116 contain only Assigned origin, with no assigned value or complete selection method.
Native IT.ADLBC.VISIT explicitly declares predecessor LB.VISIT, corroborated by workbook Variables row 119. That omitted Origin description documents the executable copy.

Native IT.ADLBC.VISITNUM explicitly declares predecessor LB.VISITNUM with precision 1, corroborated by workbook Variables row 120. This documents the source and precision used by the executable derivation despite their omission from the reading-copy Origin projection.

Native IT.ADLBC.PARAMCD explicitly declares predecessor LB.TESTCD, corroborated by workbook Variables row 122. The retained LB schema and executable derivation instead use LB.LBTESTCD, so the issue is a documented source-name discrepancy rather than absence of documentation.

ADLBC.PARCAT1's section lists CHEM, HEM and HYLAW, while native IT.ADLBC.PARCAT1 and workbook Variables row 124 only declare Assigned origin with no assigned value. ADRG page-12 limits the dataset to chemistry but does not state the constant PARCAT1='CHEM' assignment.

Native IT.ADLBC.AVAL explicitly declares predecessor LB.LBSTRESN, corroborated by workbook Variables row 125. That omitted Origin description documents the executable source; no ADLBC value-level override was found.
ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE without a visit-number condition. The executable VISITNUM <> 1 branch adds an eligibility restriction absent from the full retained method and native workbook.

ADLBC.ANL01FL gives an unqualified max(ALBTRVAL), and ADRG page-12 describes dataset structure without defining the maximum's partition. Neither the retained sections nor the native workbook identifies STUDYID/USUBJID/PARAMCD as its aggregation keys.

ADLBC.ANL01FL does not restrict its maximum to visits 4 through 12 or exclude unscheduled assessments. ADRG page-8's general statement that unscheduled visits were used does not supply RK_ANL's candidate filter.

ADLBC.ANL01FL states only the conditional Y assignment, leaving other character-flag results unassigned. Serializing those missing character results as empty text in ANL01FL's final branch adds no distinct clinical category or selection rule.

ADLBC.ANL01FL does not state the partition or eligible records for max(ALBTRVAL). ADRG page-12 and the native workbook do not resolve those choices, so a complete probe would require an added aggregation scope.

ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states a maximum but gives no rule for a partially missing pair of signed operands. ALBTRVAL's any-null guard chooses propagation in that case, and the full native range metadata does not document that policy.

ADLBC.ANRIND's method ends with the otherwise N result. Under yamaa null comparisons neither threshold condition is true for missing AVAL, so the explicit AVAL IS NULL -> N branch repeats that fallback rather than adding a new result category.

ADLBC.ANRIND names LBSTRNHI, which is absent from the native LB declarations and staged schema. ADLBC.A1HI supports a possible spelling repair to LBSTNRHI, but a literal executable rule cannot silently make that repair or replace the documented Y and multiplier.

ADLBC.BNRIND uses unqualified range-limit names without selecting their source record. Neither its full method nor native workbook specifies the BL lookup keyed by subject/test and restricted by LBBLFL='Y'.

ADLBC.BNRIND's full method gives low/high tests and an N fallback, with no rule returning missing when BASE is missing. The explicit BASE IS NULL -> empty-text branch therefore adds a missing-value assignment.

ADLBC.BNRIND's low branch assigns ANRIND rather than BNRIND, and its high-limit source LBSTRNHI is undefined in the native LB metadata and data. The method also fails to specify which record supplies the range limits, so a literal BNRIND probe would require repairs and a source-record choice.

Native IT.ADLBC.ABLFL explicitly declares predecessor LB.LBBLFL, corroborated by workbook Variables row 138. The executable first_available copy merely serializes missing character flags as empty text; its source rule is documented.

ADLBC.AENTMTFL describes the treatment phase without RK_ENT's numeric analysis-visit boundaries or blanket exclusion of unscheduled assessments. The retained ADRG statements and native workbook do not supply those candidate restrictions.

ADLBC.AENTMTFL does not specify how tied final assessments receive the flag. RK_ENT's dense ranking retains all records tied at its highest eligible AVISITN, a concrete tie policy absent from the retained methods.

ADLBC.AENTMTFL supplies conditional Y assignments and otherwise leaves the character flag unassigned. The final empty-text branch serializes that ordinary missing result without adding a new flag category or selection rule.

ADLBC.AENTMTFL and its duplicate under AVISIT do not define the treatment-period boundaries, early-discontinuation predicate or last-assessment ordering. ADRG pages 8 and 12 plus native SUPPLB.ENDPOINT's 'see SAP' declaration do not complete those selection rules.
Native IT.ADLBC.LBSEQ explicitly declares predecessor LB.LBSEQ, corroborated by workbook Variables row 140. That omitted Origin description documents the executable copy.

Native IT.ADLBC.LBNRIND explicitly declares predecessor LB.LBNRIND, corroborated by workbook Variables row 141. The executable first_available copy preserves that rule while serializing missing character values as empty text.

Native IT.ADLBC.LBSTRESN explicitly declares predecessor LB.LBSTRESN, corroborated by workbook Variables row 142. That omitted Origin description documents the executable copy and has no ADLBC value-level override.

ADLBC.ADT names LB.LBDTC as the Analysis Date source, ADRG page-45 retains ADT as Date, and native IT.ADLBC.ADT supplies DATE9. format. The ISO date-prefix extraction at adlbc.yaml line 357 implements that documented calendar-date conversion; it adds no imputation or clinical record-selection rule.
